payload.reason: The evidence explains that prior knowledge distillation techniques are ineffective for student models with different vocabularies because they require the student and teacher models to share the same vocabulary and output space, which limits their ability to reduce model sizes effectively.

claims.text: Knowledge distillation techniques cannot yield student models with different vocabularies because they require shared vocabularies and output spaces, limiting their effectiveness.
The student vocabulary may tokenize words differently than the teacher vocabulary, leading to misalignment in outputs, which hampers the effectiveness of existing distillation techniques.
Existing distillation methods rely on the alignment of output spaces, which is not possible when the student model has a different vocabulary and embedding dimensions.
